payload.claim: Several line-number citations into saffron/phases/package.py in the 'Out of scope' and 'Notes for the agent' sections are stale by roughly 49 lines (apparently read before SA-0329 shifted the file) and point at unrelated code at this snapshot. For example: 'PACKAGE's own lease push over a carried pull request (saffron/phases/package.py:913-919)' actually sits at lines 962-968; 'Update the docstring sentence at saffron/phases/package.py:1067-1070' (repeated as ':1068-1070 names two states') actually names lines 1067-1070, which are the link=result.pr_url/note=result.note kwargs inside _finish's QueueLine(...) call, not the push_unpackaged_work docstring sentence, whose real location is lines 1117-1119; 'A repo_id of None still reads no rows (:1140-1144)' is really at 1189-1193; 'the open-pull-request guard reads others (:1145-1155)' is really at 1194-1204; 'The comment at :1146 names EXHAUSTED alone' and 'the guard at :1147-1151 refuses on neither of its two shapes' are really at 1195-1200; 'The note at :1153 says awaiting review' is really at line 1202; 'The branch check reads every row's pushed_sha (:1157-1162)' is really at 1206-1211; and the Out-of-scope citation '_finish writes an empty pr_url and pushed_sha over a carried pull request (:998-1005)' for the conflict path is really at lines 801-814 (998-1005 is the open_draft_pr/_finish call for READY_FOR_REVIEW). This same revision correctly fixed two analogous stale citations elsewhere in the Context section (_finish now cited at the correct :1043-1075, and _state's location added at the correct :682-683), which shows the drift is known and partially remediated but left uncorrected in the rest of the document for the same file. None of this affects the mechanical mutants or witnesses, which all use literal find/replace text rather than line numbers, and the spec does carry a general instruction ('Lines cited here were read before it [SA-0329], so find each by its text') that mitigates the risk, but a cell or operator trusting the stale docstring-location citation literally would edit the wrong code (production code inside _finish) rather than push_unpackaged_work's docstring.
